subject: Usage discrepancy: March Marketplace invoice & entitlement mapping
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@acme-analytics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood-inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: billing@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 07:15:00 -0700
Subject: Usage spike on March AWS Marketplace invoice / entitlement mismatch

Hi Tessa / Monica,

We received our March Marketplace invoice this morning and there is a ~42% spike compared to the estimated usage in our dashboard. Our procurement team sees a large number of meter events attributed to the "acme-automation" API key that was meant to be gated under our seat-limited entitlement. The attachment is a PDF extract from our billing portal showing the line items.

Can you confirm whether Redwood applied the correct entitlement mapping for the ACME-Prod tenant after last week's deployment? If there's a known backfill or mapping issue on your side, we need a preliminary estimate of credit and a timeline for remediation — procurement needs this to approve a short-term budget hold.

Also: we flagged this with AWS billing but were told the seller (you) is the right contact for entitlement mapping issues.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Analytics

Attachments: usage_report_mar_2027.pdf (PDF, 180KB)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood-inference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood-inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage spike on March AWS Marketplace invoice / entitlement mismatch

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and the attachment. Sorry you're seeing this disruption. We're looking into it now.

Quick summary of next steps from our side: 
- Marcus will pull seller-side metering logs and cross-check the ACME-Prod tenant ID and API key mappings.
- Karthik will validate whether the entitlement rollout (seat cap config) from the rollout on 2027-03-01 applied to the marketplace SKU variant.
- We'll produce a short reconciliation matrix and either propose a credit amount or the steps for a backdated entitlement backfill.

Tentative timeline: initial findings within 4 business hours, reconciliation doc and credit proposal within 24 hours. If that timeline works, we can lock in a call for 11:30am PT to walk through the evidence.

I've attached a first-pass export (entitlement_mapping_v2.xlsx) and a dashboard snapshot we pulled to compare.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Marketplaces & Partners
Redwood Inference

Attachments: entitlement_mapping_v2.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB); dashboard_snapshot.png (PNG, 120KB)

Subject: Re: Usage spike on March AWS Marketplace invoice / entitlement mismatch

Tessa / team — quick findings from seller metering:
- There was a rollout on 2027-03-01 that introduced a SKU alias for the seat-limited offering. During that rollout, the mapping rule that maps the ACME-Prod tenant attribute (tenant_id: acme-prod-001) to the seat-capped entitlement SKU was inadvertently scoped to the internal SKU alias (sku_internal_v3) but not to the marketplace SKU name used by AWS (redwood-marketplace-saas-v2).
- Result: ~2.8M meter events from 2027-03-02 through 2027-03-07 were recorded against the public marketplace SKU without the seat cap enforcement — these events look like they carried the API key acme-automation-xx.

Proposed remediation:
1) Run a seller-side backfill that reattributes the 2.8M events to the seat-capped SKU (audit trail + signature). This allows us to request a proration/credit from AWS marketplace team.
2) For customer-facing correctness, we'll also create a sticky entitlement override to ensure API keys tied to ACME-Prod are always capped.
3) We'll open a support case with AWS Seller Support today and include the reconciliation export for fast credit processing.

Attaching a reconciliation matrix (first-pass) and the seller-side logs excerpt.

Marcus
Revenue Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: reconciliation_matrix_firstpass.csv (CSV, 90KB)

Thanks, Tessa/Marcus. 11:30am PT works for a short sync. Procurement wants the following to be on the record ahead of the call:
- A clear candidate credit amount (USD) and whether that will be handled via an AWS Marketplace credit or a direct seller credit.
- Confirmation that new automation (we rolled a job on 2027-03-02) is not being double-counted by any integration.
- Temporary billing hold / tender while this is under investigation — can you advise how quickly Redwood can request a formal credit from AWS?

We prefer the marketplace credit route if possible (easiest for our accounting), but will accept seller-side credit if AWS declines.

See you at 11:30.

Elena
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood-inference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@acme-analytics.com>, billing@acme-analytics.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood-inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>, aws-seller.support@amazon.com
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage spike on March AWS Marketplace invoice / entitlement mismatch

Thanks all — recap and resolution path we will execute: 

1) Short sync scheduled: 11:30am PT (we met and reviewed logs; minutes below).
2) Candidate credit: based on seller-side reattribution, estimated customer-impactful overcount is $14,320. We will submit that as a Marketplace credit request to AWS (case already opened, ref: HS-12093), and simultaneously offer a temporary seller credit if AWS requires additional processing time.
3) Timeline:
   - Seller backfill job scheduled (non-blocking) to reattribute meter events by EOD 2027-03-08.
   - AWS seller support case submission: done (inc 3 CSVs + reconciliation matrix). Expected AWS review window 2–5 business days, we will push for expedited review and tag as \"billing impact\".
   - Customer-facing entitlement fix (sticky override) deployed and validated within 2 hours post-backfill.
4) Billing hold: we do not control AWS invoice generation, but we will request AWS to place a pro-forma hold and prioritize the credit. Meanwhile Redwood will flag the invoice in our internal partner dashboard and provide procurement with the credit request confirmation to support your accounting hold.

Next steps (owner):
- Marcus: finalize and deliver the reconciliation CSV and logs to Elena and cc AWS (done).
- Karthik: deploy entitlement override and provide validation screenshots (in progress).
- Tessa: follow up with AWS seller support and send the official credit request packet to billing@acme-analytics.com.

Links: reconciliation export and evidence: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFGHjk-example (shared with Elena)
AWS case: HS-12093

I'll update this thread when we have confirmation from AWS. Apologies again for the noise — we'll make this right.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Marketplaces & Partners
Redwood Inference

Attachments (sent to AWS & Acme): usage_report_mar_2027.pdf; entitlement_mapping_v2.xlsx; reconciliation_matrix_firstpass.csv
